notes: Measured on synthetic fixtures with a key kept in this repository. BenchmarkPython (Flask, 2463 routes) matched its decorator count in Phase 2, but no recall figure for planted flaws has been taken on a blind key yet.
Flask with SQLite: four planted authorization flaws and a fixed copy. The key was written before the first measurement.
Correction after the first measurement: the first flaw listed a second check by mistake (a copy of the delete flaw). Nothing else in the key changed.

First measurement on this fixture, before any engine change: 8 of 8 entry points, 3 of 4 flaws found, 6 findings on the fixed copy. The six were checks that did not see the decorators require_user and require_admin as a session read and a role check. The Python vocabulary now names require_* decorators; the fixed copy then gave 1 finding, a missing audit record on the admin route, which was a real gap in the fixture and was repaired in both copies. The measurement is therefore no longer blind for these two decorator names.

The read by id flaw is missed: check.authz.owner-filter-on-id-read does not find it in this layout (a Python SELECT with the id placeholder inside a function that is not in a file the check reads as a handler file).
2026-10-14: the first flaw also accepts check.map.read-by-id-without-owner, which was built in step 6c after these fixtures missed the flaw.
